videos.label: ME vs MY BRAIN

lines.t: Okay. One hour of real work. Let's go.
Sure. But first, let's check your phone. Real quick.
No. I'm working.
What if someone texted you? It could be important.
Nobody texted me.
Fine. Then let's reorganise your desk. And your whole life.
Here's the trick. Phone in another room. Then I only promise two minutes.
Two minutes? Okay. That's nothing.
Forty minutes later.
Send this to someone whose brain does the same thing.

videos.label: NOTES
videos.heading: things nobody tells you about focus
lines: Things nobody tells you about focus.
Focus is not a personality trait. It's an environment.
Tired focus and bored focus need different fixes. Rest for one. A harder task for the other.
Starting is the hardest part. After ten minutes, it gets easier.
Your phone doesn't have to ring to steal your attention. It just has to be visible.
One finished task beats five started ones.
Save this for the next time you think you're lazy.

videos.label: FOCUS QUIZ
lines: Focus quiz. Three questions. Keep score.

lines.t: Question one. Multitasking helps you get more done. True or false?
lines.q: Multitasking helps you get more done.

lines.t: False. Every switch costs you time and attention. Your brain is switching, not multitasking.
Question two. After an interruption, getting back into deep focus can take over twenty minutes. True or false?
lines.q: Getting back into deep focus after an interruption can take 20+ minutes.

lines.t: True. Research on office workers found it often takes more than twenty minutes to get back on track.
Question three. Your phone only distracts you when it rings. True or false?
lines.q: Your phone only distracts you when it buzzes.

lines.t: False. Studies suggest just having it in sight can pull at your attention.

lines: How many did you get? Comment your score out of three.
videos.title: Focus quiz: only 1 in 10 gets 3/3
videos.caption: Focus quiz 🧠 How many did you get right? Comment your score /3 👇 #focusquiz #howtofocus #adhd #productivity #studytips

videos.label: RANKED
lines: Five focus rules from my system, ranked.

lines.t: Number five. Plan tomorrow tonight. Zero decisions in the morning.
Number four. Three lists. Today, later, never. Only look at today.
Number three. Twenty-five minutes on, five off, twenty-five on.
Number two. One sticky note. One task. Until it's done.
And number one. Phone in another room. Not face down. Another room.
